Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
124 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 123 AM EST Tuesday...

No significant changes were made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 123 AM EST Tuesday...

1. Dry weather continues with a warming trend expected through 
the end of this week.

2. The weekend will start off on a dry note, with chances for 
showers returning by the end of the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 123 AM EST Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Low level moisture trapped beneath an inversion 
has led to low clouds over the Adirondacks overnight. We also 
have some fog forming in the valleys where the skies have 
cleared as surface high pressure is in control of our weather 
with light winds. Center of surface high pressure will remain 
nearly stationary to the southwest of our region, but this will 
provide us with very quiet weather through this week. 
Temperatures will be about 10 degrees above seasonal normals 
during the day, and about 5 degrees above normal at night. Each 
day we should have partly to mostly sunny skies, with mainly 
clear nights as well.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Our nice clear and dry stretch will hold on for 
one more day this weekend on Saturday before shower chances 
return for Sunday into Monday. Temperatures Saturday will be 
similar to that of the work week with highs in the mid to upper 
50s and generally clear skies as a secondary ridge, associated 
with our overarching high passes through. The high centered over
the Mid-Atlantic will slide east, but models remain uncertain 
as to how much the high departs, in addition to how much it 
weakens. This will play a role for our shower chances Sunday 
into Monday. There is strong model agreement that a coastal low 
will develop off the Carolina coast Sunday. However, models 
begin to diverge on the track of the system towards next week. 
The GFS and notably the Google AI Deepmind phase this system 
with an approaching Great Lakes shortwave late Sunday bringing 
widespread shower chances from south to north; the steadiest of 
which is focused over southern Vermont. This track depicts the 
departing high as keeping its strength off the east coast, 
amplifying the Great Lakes shortwave, and dragging the coastal 
low north into our region. Conversely, the ECMWF and CMC weaken 
the departing high, keeping our pattern more progressive, and 
tracking the coastal low out to see, more near Benchmark. This 
leaves us with a weaker Great Lakes shortwave, which favors 
lighter showers mainly across the Adirondacks and areas near the
International Border. Currently consensus favors the latter of 
the two solutions, but we will closely monitor trends for the 
weekend into next week. Regardless, our temperatures will return
to seasonable levels to start off next week with highs back 
into the 40s.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 06Z Wednesday...Great Lakes moisture has arrived at SLK
a few hours earlier than model guidance, but expectations are 
that these IFR clouds will persist at least towards 15Z or so, 
similarly to yesterday, before ceilings improve back towards VFR
by 16/17Z today. In Vermont, valley fog has developed in the CT
river and some localized areas around EFK/MPV. While persistent
fog is not anticipated due to some drier conditions at MPV/EFK,
with crossover temperatures already crossed, and fog evident on
satellite, confidence has increased slightly with pattern 
recognition favoring some period of fog potential near sunrise 
this morning. Have used VCFG with a tempo of 2 hours or so for 
IFR near sunrise for MPV/EFK. Outside of SLK/MPV/EFK, cigs will 
remain VFR through the TAF period, with winds across the region 
remaining south to southwest, except at RUT where more westerly 
winds are expected. After 14/15Z, sustained winds between 10-15 
kts with gusts around 20 knots can be expected at MSS before 
winds subside after 22/23Z.
